evidence.reference_title: Can successful pregnancy be achieved and predicted from patients with identified ZP mutations? A literature review.
evidence.snippet: Sixty-nine mutations of the ZP genes were reported in 87 patients with different clinical phenotypes, including empty follicle syndrome (EFS), ZP-free oocytes (ZFO), ZP-thin oocytes (ZTO), degenerated and immature oocytes. The phenotypes of patients were influenced by the types and location of the mutations. The most common effects of ZP mutations are protein truncation and dysfunction. Three patients with ZP1 mutations, two with ZP2 mutations, and three with ZP4 mutations had successful pregnancies through Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) from ZFO or ZTO.

nodes.description: In healthy human oocytes, secreted ZP2, ZP3, and ZP4 polymerize into long filaments that are covalently cross-linked into a stable three-dimensional extracellular matrix via intermolecular disulfide bonds (mediated by conserved Cys66 in chicken ZP1 and the corresponding Cys77 in the N-terminal ZP-N1 domain of human ZP1) forming ZP1-N1 homodimers, while human ZP4-N1 remains monomeric and cannot substitute for ZP1 cross-linking. Pathogenic ZP1 variants either eliminate secreted ZP1, disrupt ZP1-N1 homodimerization (such as p.Trp83Arg and p.Arg109His), alter the trefoil or ZP domains, or abolish heteromeric interaction with ZP2 and ZP3, resulting in a markedly thinned, fragile, or completely absent zona pellucida matrix.

nodes.description: During ovarian folliculogenesis, the zona pellucida provides the structural scaffold that stabilizes transzonal projections and gap-junctional communication between surrounding cumulus granulosa cells and the growing primary oocyte. In ZP1-deficient follicles, preantral follicles initially form a thin ZP composed of ZP2, ZP3, and ZP4 without ZP1; however, as follicles expand into the antral stage and antral cavity fluid accumulates, the uncross-linked ZP separates from surrounding granulosa cells, cumulus-oocyte complex (COC) architecture collapses, and bidirectional nutrient and paracrine signaling between cumulus granulosa cells and the oocyte is disrupted.

The eggs of Zp1MT/MT females were not surrounded by a ZP and lost their fertilization capacity in vitro. Zp1MT/MT females mated with wild-type males failed to become pregnant.

nodes.description: Unlike humans and rats, mice possess only three functional zona pellucida genes (Zp1, Zp2, and Zp3, with Zp4 pseudogenized). Homozygous Zp1-null female mice still assemble a loosely organized, porous zona pellucida matrix composed of mZP2 and mZP3, with ectopic clusters of granulosa cells trapped in the perivitelline space. Zp1-null female mice remain fertile with reduced litter sizes (~50% of wild-type) due to fragile cleavage-stage embryos and precocious hatching in the oviduct, making the mouse knock-out a milder structural phenotype than the truncating/missense ZP1 mutations seen in humans and knock-in rats.

In some Zp1 null follicles, this structural abnormality resulted in ectopic clusters of granulosa cells, lodged between the zona matrix and the oolemma, that perturbed normal folliculogenesis. Comparable numbers of eggs were ovulated from Zp1 null females and normal females following hormonal stimulation. However, after mating with males, fewer two-cell embryos were recovered from Zp1 null females, and their litters were significantly smaller than those produced by normal mice.

evidence.reference_title: Mutant ZP1 in familial infertility.
evidence.snippet: Sequencing of candidate genes ZP1, ZP2, ZP3, and ZP4 revealed that six members of generation IV (the four patients and two unmarried family members) carried a homozygous frameshift deletion of 8 bp encompassing nucleotides 1169 through 1176 in ZP1 (GenBank accession number, KJ489454).

nodes.description: Missense variant in the N-terminal ZP-N1 domain (c.247T>C, p.Trp83Arg) that reduces hZP1-N1 secretion and disrupts intermolecular disulfide-bonded homodimerization required for human ZP filament cross-linking.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular basis of egg coat cross-linking sheds light on ZP1-associated female infertility.
evidence.snippet: Consistent with an important role of W72 in the folding and dimerisation of cZP1-N1, this experiment showed that W83R not only decreases the secretion of hZP1-N1 but also significantly reduces its ability to form disulphide-bonded homodimers (Fig. 7b). This suggests that the mutation leads to lack of the ZP by hindering human ZP filament cross-linking.

nodes.description: N-terminal ZP-N1 cross-linking domain missense variant that impairs ZP1 secretion and cross-linking function, reported in heterozygous state in a woman with ZP-free oocytes who achieved live birth after ICSI.

evidence.reference_title: Heterozygous mutations in ZP1 and ZP3 cause formation disorder of ZP and female infertility in human.
evidence.snippet: Here, we performed whole-exome sequencing in two probands with primary infertility whose oocytes lacked a ZP, and we identified a heterozygous mutation in ZP1 (NM_207341:c.326G>A p.Arg109His), which is situated in the N-terminus, and a heterozygous mutation in ZP3 (NM_001110354:c.400G>A p.Ala134Thr), which is situated in the ZP domain.

nodes.description: Paternally inherited heterozygous missense variant in the trefoil domain of ZP1 (c.785A>G, p.Tyr262Cys) that introduces an unpaired cysteine, impairs ZP1 glycosylation and secretion, and causes abnormal zona pellucida formation.

evidence.reference_title: ZP1-Y262C mutation causes abnormal zona pellucida formation and female infertility in humans.
evidence.snippet: In a patient (II-1) displaying abnormal zona pellucida formation, we successfully identified the heterozygous ZP1 mutation (ZP1-Y262C) via whole-exome sequencing.
